ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Pablo Neruda

code.originalText: Four-week review on apalutamide and leuprolide: early PSA response, testosterone, blood pressure, pain, the dental check and the first denosumab dose, and the radiotherapy plan

text.paragraph: Four-week review on apalutamide and leuprolide. [S]

Mr. Neruda returns four weeks after starting apalutamide and three weeks after his first leuprolide injection, with a professional Spanish interpreter. The right hip pain has eased to 2 of 10 and no longer wakes him; he takes acetaminophen once a day at most. He gets up to pass urine twice a night instead of three times. Mild hot flashes began last week. His energy is a little lower in the afternoons. He has had no rash, falls, dizziness, leg weakness or numbness. He saw his dentist a week ago; no dental work is needed. He takes vitamin D every day. The germline test result came back last week: no harmful variant was found. He had his radiotherapy planning visit, and treatment starts in two weeks. Before radiotherapy, his bowels are regular, once a day, with no bleeding. [S]

tr.td: Well; walks without favoring the right hip

Adenocarcinoma of the prostate, Grade Group 4 (Gleason 4+4), cT3a N1 M1b, de novo metastatic hormone-sensitive disease, low volume by conventional imaging (two bone metastases, in the right ilium and L5, and two pelvic lymph nodes; no visceral disease); synthetic modern detail linked to his documented prostate cancer of 1971

Pelvic lymph node metastases: right external iliac and right obturator nodes

list.item:
Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer on leuprolide and apalutamide (C61). Early response: PSA 46.8 to 6.2 ng/mL, testosterone 22 ng/dL (castrate), alkaline phosphatase falling to 141 U/L, and less pain. The germline panel shows no pathogenic variant, so cascade testing of relatives is not needed; somatic testing of the biopsy is pending. [S]
Continue apalutamide 240 mg daily.
Radiotherapy to the prostate from two weeks' time.
Second leuprolide injection and three-month PSA at the next visit.

Hypertension, higher on apalutamide (I10). 152/90 mm Hg, up from 142/86, as expected when apalutamide speeds the breakdown of amlodipine. [S]
Amlodipine raised from 5 mg to 10 mg daily.
Home blood pressure readings sent through the portal in two weeks.

Low bone mass with high fracture risk (M85.89). Calcium 9.3 mg/dL; vitamin D 28 ng/mL and rising; dental examination clear. [S]
Denosumab 60 mg subcutaneously today, then every six months.
Continue cholecalciferol 2000 units daily; report numbness around the mouth or muscle cramps.

Androgen deprivation with apalutamide (Z79.899). Mild hot flashes and fatigue. TSH 2.4 mIU/L today; the baseline before apalutamide was not drawn. [S]
TSH every four months on apalutamide.
Report any rash early.

Follow-up: Radiotherapy from two weeks' time. Home blood pressure readings through the portal in two weeks. Review in nine weeks, at three months, with PSA, testosterone, blood count, chemistry, TSH and hemoglobin A1c, and the second leuprolide injection. Next scheduled visit 2026-09-14: three-month review: PSA and testosterone, thyroid function, blood count and chemistry, glucose, radiotherapy effects, the rash, the second leuprolide injection, and plans for the year. [S]
